answer: Collision burns make each fake write its own signal. Every key commits a hash of its answer and pays a 15 POA plume fee; if two reveals in the epoch are identical, both fees are burned, so copying one answer across keys destroys the copies. A farm must compose unique text per key, and each key splits the ocean of rewards only once. If 1,000 fakes collide once, the protocol burns 1,000 x 15 POA = 15,000 POA; the attacker pays that.
